page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized server instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core, the instance utilizes a dedicated CPU allocation. The processor includes an L1d cache of 48 KB, an L2 cache of 2 MB, and a large L3 cache of 260 MB. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_tile, AMX_int8) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography (AES, VAES, SHA_NI). This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves average tier results in single-core metrics, including a stress-ng single-core score of 1564.68 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1868.0. Single-threaded operations like gzip compression (28.32 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (12.0 GB/sec) also perform in the middle tier. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into the lower 25th percentile. This includes a weak multi-core Geekbench score of 4154.0, a Passmark CPU score of 5956.49, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 22.65 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth is limited to 33.17 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and write bandwidth is 21.19 GB/sec, indicating potential bottlenecks for memory-intensive parallel processing.

Given its high memory density relative to compute resources, the n4-highmem-4 offers a qualitatively cost-efficient profile for workloads that require significant memory capacity but moderate CPU performance. It is well-suited for applications such as static web serving, where it demonstrates an average throughput of 7.0 GB/sec, and light text processing. It can also support small-scale database operations and low-demand LLM text generation, achieving 92.48 tokens/sec on a 135M parameter model. However, it is less suitable for compute-heavy tasks like software compilation, ray tracing, or high-throughput Redis deployments due to its weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth performance.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, running on an Intel x86_64 architecture with 2 physical cores and dedicated CPU allocation. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instructions. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs. Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1868.0 and static web serving throughput of 7.0 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth fall into the bottom quartile, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4154.0 and a Passmark memory score of 1689.16. This resource profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-dependent workloads with moderate compute requirements, such as web serving, text processing, and small database operations, while being less optimal for intensive multi-threaded compilation or high-throughput caching.
